what: Rotate Video turns a video by 90 or 180 degrees, or mirrors or flips it, and saves it as a new MP4 file.

Phones sometimes record with the wrong orientation, and selfie videos are often mirrored. A preview on the page shows exactly how the video will look before you save it. The picture itself is turned, so it plays the right way up in every player, website and app.
The video is processed in your browser with FFmpeg compiled to WebAssembly and is never uploaded.
uses: Fix a video that plays on its side on a computer or TV.
Turn a video filmed with the phone upside down.
Un-mirror a front-camera video so writing reads correctly.
Make a portrait video landscape, or the other way round.
Flip footage for a reflection effect.
tutorial: Click the box or drop a video onto it. The name, size, length and picture size are shown, and the video starts playing silently in the preview.
Press "90° right", "90° left", "Upside down (180°)", "Mirror (left-right)" or "Flip (top-bottom)". The preview turns at once.
The hint shows the new picture size and whether it will be portrait or landscape.
"Good" is recommended. "High" keeps more detail in a bigger file; "Smaller file" is easier to share.
Press "Rotate video", wait for the progress bar, then press "Download video". The name shows what was done, such as trip-rotated-right.mp4.
features: See the turned video before saving.
The pixels are turned, so every player shows it correctly.
The sound track is kept, copied without change when possible.
Plays on phones, computers, TVs and social media.

example.title: Worked example: a sideways school play
example.text: Omar filmed his daughter's school play holding the phone sideways, and on the laptop the stage is on its side with the top on the left. He drops play.mp4 on the box and presses "90° right". The preview now shows the stage upright and the hint says the new video will be 1920 × 1080 (landscape). He presses "Rotate video" and downloads play-rotated-right.mp4.

tips: If the top of the picture is on the left, choose 90° right; if it is on the right, 90° left.
Use "Mirror" for selfie videos where text appears backwards.
Cut the video with the Video Trimmer first if you only need part of it; it will be faster.
Choose "Smaller file" quality for long videos you want to send by chat.
problems: Your browser cannot play this format (common for MKV and AVI). Choose the turn anyway; the result is an MP4 that plays everywhere.
The video still looks sideways in one app
Make sure you opened the new downloaded file, not the original.
The whole video has to be re-encoded. Shorter videos and "Smaller file" are faster, and a computer is faster than a phone.
Try a shorter video or a computer.
